Mercedes Rolls Out MANUFAKTUR-Infused SL 55 2026 WTA Finals Winner’s Car
6 photos
Photo: Mercedes-AMG
Mercedes and its AMG division have found another way to sell the appeal of the MANUFAKTUR customization program. On this occasion, the happy customer happens to be the winner of a tennis tournament. Described as a one-off, this SL 55 4MATIC+ is destined for the WTA Finals champ.
Beautified with ultraviolet paintwork over white Nappa leather, the 55 in question boasts a bunch of personalized goodies that connect it to the Women's Tennis Association. The roadster was unleashed in the flesh at Merc's Brand Studio in Beverly Hills right before the competition starts in Indian Wells.
As you can tell from the shots provided by none other than Mercedes , the exterior does most of the talking. The look-at-me paintwork is a MANUFAKTUR Made to Measure finish inspired by the WTA's purple. 21-inch AMG forged cross-spoke wheels add no subtlety whatsoever. On the contrary, these wheels make the German roadster even more audacious.
Subtlety, however, was never the assignment. In fact, Merc was fully aware that it had to deliver a car that looks precisely like a tournament prize before anyone gets close enough to see its Mercedes-Benz and Mercedes-AMG badging. This audacity continues inside, where Crystal White MANUFAKTUR Nappa leather does the talking by creating a sharp contrast.
AMG carbon-fiber trim pieces add to the visual drama, bringing some darker surfaces into the mix. WTA Finals embossing and engraving remind the owner that she did not simply take delivery of just another 55. The special treatment continues with custom door sills and a special badge that will ultimately carry the winner's name, giving this SL an identity of its own, beyond the crazy paint job and the superb-looking upholstery.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG There is, however, a problem with this car that I cannot ignore. Why 55 and not the 63 or something even more special? For model year 2027, the AMG SL range is topped by a plug-in hybrid with ridiculous torque, and this powertrain is exactly what I would expect from such a collab between the Stuttgart-based automaker and the Women's Teams Association.
It gets worse once you remember that Mercedes and the AMG division also gave Maybach a shot at the SL. While it may not be as punchy as the AMG-ified 63 S E PERFORMANCE, the 680 Monogram Series is an ultra-luxury interpretation of the rear-biased roadster from Bremen.
Despite not being tuned for superlative performance, 4.0 seconds flat to 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour) is properly quick. As of this writing, the 2027 model year Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series will set you back a cool $225,900 before destination and optional extras. All in all, yeah, limiting the tournament prize to the AMG SL 55 4MATIC+ is a bit strange.
And looking at the bigger picture, this car exists because this partnership gives Mercedes a visible way to connect its name with a very popular sport and women. BMW's rival entered the 2026 season as a Premier Partner and Exclusive Automobile Partner of the WTA Tour, with this arrangement including the Signature Court, digital content, and experiences designed specifically to bring the brand closer to tennis fans.
The singles champion won't be the only player receiving something from Mercedes. Per the WTA, each member of the winning doubles team will receive a complimentary 12-month lease of a Mercedes-Benz vehicle. That being said, the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals run from November 8, 2026, through November 15, 2026, and this edition marks the competition's first visit to the California venue.
